tldr: The Agentic Web is a new phase of the internet in which autonomous AI agents powered by LLMs act on behalf of users, coordinating with one another to plan, execute, and complete complex tasks—marking a shift from human-driven to machine-to-machine web interactions.
contributions: Defines and formalizes the concept of the Agentic Web as a distributed, interactive internet ecosystem where autonomous agents serve as intermediaries for goal-directed tasks
Traces the evolution of the Web across three eras: PC Web, Mobile Web, and the emerging Agentic Web
Proposes a three-dimensional conceptual model (intelligence, interaction, and economics) to frame the dynamics of the Aggent Web
Reinterprets foundational Web concepts (PageRank, search, recommender systems, crawlers) through the lens of agent autonomy and collaboration
Discusses architectural challenges, applications, societal risks, and governance issues of agentic systems
Provides a continuously updated repository of relevant studies at https://github.com/SafeRL-Lab/agentic-web
methods: This is a conceptual and survey-style paper that synthesizes existing literature on LLM-powered agents, search, recommendation systems, and multi-agent coordination to define and structure the Agentic Web paradigm. The authors review the historical evolution of the Web across three eras (PC Web, Mobile Web, Agentic Web), propose a three-dimensional framework (intelligence, interaction, economics), and analyze architectural and infrastructural challenges for scalable agentic systems. They illustrate the paradigm through concrete examples (flight booking and deep research tasks) and reinterpret classic Web technologies (PageRank, crawlers, yellow pages) in the context of agent-mediated interactions.
results: The paper establishes the Agentic Web as a paradigm where autonomous agents can handle complex, long-horizon, multi-step tasks on behalf of users without manual intervention. Key findings include: (1) the transition from static, keyword-based search (PC Web) to recommendation-driven consumption (Mobile Web) to action-driven agent delegation (Agentic Web); (2) agents can access knowledge embedded in LLM parameters directly, combine it with real-time retrieval, and proactively recommend content beyond traditional search; (3) webpages evolve into active software agents with capabilities, interfaces, and roles; hyperlinks become coordination channels; (4) foundational concepts like PageRank must be reinterpreted to reflect agent utility, responsiveness, and cooperation potential; (5) agent metadata may include standardized schemas for APIs, trust levels, performance benchmarks, and negotiation protocols; (6) the paper identifies an emerging 'Agent Attention Economy' and discusses agent registries/marketplaces as replacements for traditional web directories.
limitations: The paper is primarily conceptual and survey-based, lacking empirical validation, quantitative evaluations, or implemented system benchmarks for the Agentic Web framework. It acknowledges a 'noticeable gap in the current literature' in systematically analyzing and redefining web fundamentals for an agent-driven future, suggesting the work is exploratory rather than conclusive. Many proposals (e.g., agent crawlers, agent registries, reinterpreted PageRank) remain speculative and unvalidated.
